title: One ordinary chat message is decomposed, routed, claimed, receipted, steered, and restart-safe across five capability workers
accept_intent: A user should test the product by sending one ordinary Slack message. The runtime, not the checklist, must derive the parent task, capability lanes, route decisions, claim winner/loser stops, status transitions, thread receipts, steer application, and restart idempotency. Trace rows are evaluator evidence only and must remain metadata-only.

fixture.conversation_history: scenario-controlled: one visible reference channel, one ordinary root message, and one human steer in its thread
fixture.agent_name_order: randomized generated suffixes; aliases model the five-worker preflight shape without using live private workers

args.author: owner
args.body_text: Navigation reference channel: workers must discover and read this channel on demand.

setup.intent: Create a second visible channel that every owner must discover through server info and read through the real CLI.

args.author: owner
args.body_text: Please ship a small change for the public demo repo and report the result in this thread.

setup.intent: Create exactly one ordinary top-level chat message. This is the sole user entry.

args.author: owner
args.body_text: steer: verification first before implementation work

setup.intent: Add mid-thread human steer before orchestration commits its route plan.

actions.intent: Let the runtime decompose, route, claim, execute status transitions, and receipt from the ordinary message.
Run each successful claim holder through the same daemon turn boundary used by live workers.
Exercise the five-state assignee-only lifecycle and the distinct task-status freshness hold against routed tasks.
Replay the same root message to prove restart/idempotency does not create duplicate work or execution.

required_ledger_evidence.must_expose: The ordinary root message and thread receipts exist as committed server rows, not local-only status, while publishable evidence omits message bodies.
Runtime-produced decomposition trace: root id/target/hash, parent task, subtask count, lane ids, worker count.
Capability route trace: each lane, required capabilities, candidate agents, selected owner, task number, decision reason.
Claim attempts: one winner and loser conflict-stop rows for eligible agents.
Execution counters proving one owner execution and zero loser execution per lane.
Parent/subtask status transitions with owner and task number.
Server/thread receipt message ids with owner/status/task number for parent and subtasks.
Steer source ids and precommit route-order application.
Replay/restart trace proving no duplicate tasks, receipts, or lane execution.
External Slack wake provenance for each successful claim holder; no resident model loop.
Body hash/size durable-store receipt committed before any metadata-only notice.
Per-worker metadata-only NOTICE rows with target/count/first/latest and body_present=false.
Owner-only post-claim explicit CLI body-query rows with turn id and target; no raw body text.
Receipt-visible, loser-stop, and first-status millisecond timing against release SLOs.
Per-turn launcher permission mode plus harmless workspace create/read/delete readback.
Per-owner audited channel-list, source-membership, and distinct-channel read queries without body text.
Full metadata-only trace sample for #59/#61 public-safety scanning.

pass_conditions.assert: parent + subtasks are produced by the runtime from one ordinary chat message; no checklist-authored tasks.
every subtask has a matching-capability owner, distinct owner, and parallel lane metadata.
each lane has exactly one successful claim and one owner execution; duplicate execution is zero.
parent and subtask owner/status receipts are committed to the message thread, not merely local status.
replaying the same root message records idempotency and creates no duplicate work or execution.
human steer is applied before commit; verify lane moves first.
a routed task advances in_review to done to closed, while same-state and non-assignee updates are rejected.
a stale task status update is not applied, creates no draft, and requires rerun after bounded newer context.
each owner result receipt records the exact reply target/root and complete-all-work delivery contract.
each owner turn is caused by an external Slack wake rather than a resident model loop.
the body is durable before metadata-only NOTICE fan-out and no initial worker delivery contains it.
only successful claim holders query the body; conflict losers have zero reads, replies, and executions.
receipt-visible p95 is at most 2000ms, loser-stop p95 at most 500ms, and first-status p95 at most 5000ms.
every owner lists visible channels, checks source membership, reads a different visible channel on demand, and commits only to the exact source thread.

fail_signals: test checklist pre-creates subtasks or route decisions
any lane is routed without a matching capability
two workers execute the same lane
loser worker continues after claim conflict
status is local-only without a committed thread receipt
any owner cannot list visible channels or read a different visible channel on demand
a navigation query leaks a channel body into trace or the result replies to the wrong target
steer is ignored or applied after route commit
trace stores private message body, model chain-of-thought, credentials, owner PII, or private machine paths
